source.title: Nonlinear Conjugate Gradients For Scaling Synchronous Distributed DNN Training
source.authors: Saurabh N. Adya; Vinay Palakkode; O. Tuzel

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer and batch-size conditions using held-out accuracy on natural-label ImageNet and CIFAR-100 tasks, bearing on V4 and V5 with different optimizers and measures from their cited studies.
record.gate_note: Own results on optimizer and batch-size variation bear on V4 and V5. The paper does not test memorization of random labels, width, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Its cited prior work is not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Own batch-size sweeps and longer-training experiments directly test V5. RMSProp versus Momentum/SGD comparisons also address V4, but the supplied text does not establish their relative held-out performance; NLCG superiority alone cannot decide V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that preconditioned NLCG improves convergence and accuracy at extremely large batches on ImageNet and CIFAR-100. Longer training reduces training suboptimality and improves test accuracy, with optimizer-dependent recovery. They also identify computational overhead and instability at very small batches.
record.recipe_differences: Uses preconditioned nonlinear conjugate gradients with a dynamic diagonal BFGS preconditioner and compares it with SGD, Momentum and RMSProp on standard image-classification training.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with batch size, epoch budget, optimizer and dataset; NLCG line search is disabled below batch size 2048 on CIFAR-100 because loss values are too noisy. Runs at CIFAR-100 batch size 16384 can diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Preconditioned NLCG outperforms SGD-based alternatives at extreme batch sizes and appears more robust to divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order preconditioned nonlinear conjugate gradients can improve large-batch optimization and held-out accuracy relative to the tested first-order methods.

record.problems: ImageNet result curves are described without uncertainty estimates; exact values are predominantly in figures. CIFAR-100 results use five experiments and standard-deviation bars, with some large variation and divergence at large batch size. The paper does not provide training-error versus test-error gaps, so its results concern held-out accuracy and batch/optimizer effects rather than measuring the gap directly.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other reported losses, wall-clock curves, throughput, and learning-rate schedule were omitted because they do not directly measure held-out accuracy or the versions' claimed generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.

Adam, language benchmarks, broader optimizer-specific tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers. The common ImageNet schedule is tuned for Momentum; equal or better adaptive-method training performance is not established.
Language models, controlled isolation of warmup or learning-rate scaling, normalization or regularization changes, and a demonstrated same-budget elimination of the extreme-batch penalty.
Dropout addition, removal, strength, and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.

missing.what: Direct RMSProp-versus-Momentum/SGD held-out comparisons at matched batch sizes and epoch budgets. Existing rows report batch trends or comparisons against NLCG, so they cannot support a V4 verdict. The supplied text does not preserve readable optimizer-specific curve values.
The authors report repeating the ImageNet study with ResNet-50 V1 and reaching the same conclusion; record this as qualitative replication evidence without inventing numerical results.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, paragraph following the Figure 6 discussion

record.verdict_notes: No V4 verdict is justified by NLCG's superiority or by missing Adam experiments. Longer-training recovery supports an exception already included in V5; it is not automatically a scope limitation. The selected best-accuracy reference lines are not matched optimizer baselines. Numerical curves cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Tests NLCG, Momentum, RMSProp and SGD on ImageNet and CIFAR-100; does not test Adam, language models, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.

Tests large-batch effects and longer training on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, including optimizer variation. Does not test language models or the normalization/regularization recipe changes named in the version.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: Resnet-50 V2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Momentum across mini-batch sizes; top-1 test accuracy measured.
rows.baseline: Best top-1 accuracy 76.9% achieved by NLCG_FR at batch size 1024; optimizer comparisons are shown in Figure 4.
rows.value: At batch sizes 16384 and lower, all optimizers are close to or greater than 75%; accuracy degrades above 16384. At batch size 65536, NLCG_FR is about 10.3% higher than Momentum; at 98304, about 19.5% higher.
rows.note: Figure 4 plots the optimizer-specific values; text states trends and differences. The fixed-epoch batch-size penalty appears, while optimizer performance differs substantially at extreme sizes.
rows.check: The fixed-budget batch penalty is explicitly observed above 16384, not merely partial. Use Momentum's smaller-batch accuracy as the baseline; 76.9% is another optimizer's selected best result. NLCG differences are percentage points.

rows.subject: Resnet-50 V2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with NLCG_FR across mini-batch sizes; top-1 test accuracy measured.
rows.baseline: Best top-1 accuracy 76.9% at batch size 1024; Momentum comparison at batch size 65536 and 98304.
rows.value: 76.9% best accuracy at batch size 1024; at batch size 65536, about 10.3% higher than Momentum; at 98304, about 19.5% higher than Momentum.
rows.note: The paper reports the best point and relative differences, not exact accuracy at each extreme batch size.
rows.check: Include the explicit within-NLCG_FR accuracy decline above 16384. Superiority to Momentum does not establish V4: NLCG is not the adaptive first-order method named there. Differences are percentage points.

source_check.correct: NLCG_FR achieves 76.9% at batch 1024. Its accuracy exceeds Momentum by about 10.3 percentage points at batch 65536 and 19.5 percentage points at batch 98304; these are accuracy differences, not relative percentage improvements. All four optimizers lose accuracy above batch 16384.
source_check.problem: The wording '10.3% higher' expresses an accuracy difference as a relative percentage improvement.
